painpoints.text: nu 0.115 drift cost three debug cycles in run 01M2WECF1835SYN194D0D3SCF4 despite `nu --ide-check` passing: `str replace` is literal-by-default (regex silently no-ops), `filter {|...}` is deprecated (stderr warning), and `path basename $f` inside parens is a parse error — pipe instead. Suggestion: a one-line nu-idioms note near the loop-script conventions, or a smoke-test lint that fails on `str replace` without `--regex`/`-r` when the pattern contains regex metacharacters, would catch this class mechanically.

The tracker_guard node originally had no stdin_source, so the requeue arm's self-run exclusion required touching `.fabro/workflows/develop/workflow.fabro` (adding `stdin_source="internal.run_id"`, mirroring the preflight node). No engine-side check validated the graph edit before the next run parses it — the workflow graph has no cheap parse-level check reachable from the implementer (no built fabro binary; `fabro validate` would need a cold build). Fix idea: a parse-level workflow-graph check (or a prebuilt binary in the sandbox) so config-tier seeds can validate graph edits without builds.

observations: Incidental seed-id mentions are a real false-live hazard: the current run's own journal planner line names fabro-29f7/fabro-6a78 (candidates it considered), which protected them from the first requeue implementation until self-run journal exclusion landed. Any future live-run detector over journals must exclude the invoking run and prefer planner-line association over whole-file grep.

Journal file mtimes are useless for recency (a checkout touches all of them at once) — the ts fields inside the JSONL records are the only reliable clock; the implementation parses them rather than trusting the filesystem.

sd updatedAt is a weak staleness clock: verification-only planner passes bump it via the claim form even when nothing changed, which is why the arm prefers claiming-journal terminal ts and only falls back to updatedAt.

painpoints.text: Evidence blob refs are single-line JSON (~42KB), and the read tools are line-oriented: read_file offset/limit and grep both truncate the MIDDLE of that one line, hiding part of the .seeds/issues.jsonl diff context behind giant unchanged seed records. Workaround was count-reconciliation (+3/-3 = claim + 2 requeues, one hunk seen). Fix idea: have evidence.nu write blob files pretty-printed/multi-line so reviewers can page within them (run 01M2WECF1835SYN194D0D3SCF4).

develop-claims' `($recs | get ts | last)` is unguarded: a ts-less journal record would crash the guard (never-fail contract risk); currently unreachable since engine journals always stamp ts, and crash direction is fail-safe. Also the 30s node timeout now bounds a full .fabro/journal scan that grows with run count.
